name: Plant Tycoon Fix Patcher
description: Fixes the supported classic Windows Plant Tycoon build: stops the old-age random-death branch and restores sounds and images the LDW release is missing.

settings.name: Fix Vanilla Bugs
settings.summary: Fixes stock bugs: a new game no longer starts at the Flower of Knowledge (Nox Orchid) prices, and saves that did are re-priced.
settings.description: Fixes bugs in the base game. A new game sets every plant's asking price before it forgets the magic plants of the save that was open (and the game opens your last save when it starts), so after a save that has found the Flower of Knowledge (Nox Orchid), a new game prices every plant at the Flower of Knowledge price, V + 3 x (V/4), though it has not found it. The magic plants are now forgotten first, so a new game gets the normal prices; finding the Flower of Knowledge still raises them. A save already priced this way is repaired the first time it loads: if it has not found the Flower of Knowledge and every species it has not discovered is at that price, those species get normal prices (V -+ Random(V/2), as a new game gives). Discovered species keep their prices, which you may have set, and a save with any other undiscovered price, or that has found the Flower of Knowledge, stays as it is.

settings.name: No old-age plant deaths
settings.summary: Plants no longer die of old age.
settings.description: Stops plants dying of old age. A plant's age starts at 0 when it is created and counts up in the game's internal age units. Once it passes 1720.0, the threshold held as a double at VA 0x4695E0 and compared at VA 0x42E21F, the plant becomes eligible to die: every update from then on calls Random(1000) at VA 0x42E231 and kills the plant when the roll lands in 0-9. That is a 1 in 100 chance, 1%, on each eligible update, and it keeps rolling for the rest of the plant's life, so a long-lived plant faces it repeatedly. Younger plants are never eligible and are unaffected either way. The patch changes one byte, the comparison operand at VA 0x42E23B, from 9 to -1. Because the branch is a signed compare, no roll in 0-999 can fall in range, so the chance becomes exactly 0 rather than merely small. The age check and the random call both still run untouched; only the death branch is now unreachable. Plants still die of neglect, disease and everything else. Touches 1 byte.

settings.name: R refreshes the seed shop
settings.summary: Press R in the Supplies store to restock the seed shelves at once (Legendary Seeds too), with the game's own odds.
settings.description: A cheat key for the Supplies store: pressing R (or r) on the store screen restocks all nine seed packets at once, using the game's own restock roll, so the odds are the stock ones. With Add new store upgrades and items, the three Legendary Seeds are rerolled too. Bought-out shelves fill again. The daily restock still comes at its usual time, and nothing extra is saved. R does nothing on any other screen.

settings.name: Add Missing Assets to LDW Version
settings.summary: Adds the sounds and images the LDW version of the game is missing, taken from the Steam version.
settings.description: Adds sounds and images the LDW download is missing, taken from the Steam version of the game and bundled with this patcher. The merge is only additive: files are copied into the modded game folder only where the game does not already have them. A game file is never replaced, and a bundled file identical to the game's own is ignored. Turning this off and patching again produces a folder without them. The executable is not changed.

settings.name: Tank and greenhouse counts
settings.summary: Shows how many of the 15 pots of the greenhouse on screen hold a living plant, how many are mature, have buds or are seedlings, and which are infested or unhealthy, in the game's own font, with an in-game on/off button.
settings.description: Adds a line along the top of the greenhouse screen: "Plants: 9 of 15 (5 mature, 2 with buds, 2 seedlings)", counting the pots of the greenhouse you are looking at (Greenhouse 1 to Greenhouse 6 with 5 extra greenhouses) that hold a living plant, and under it "Infested: 2  Unhealthy: 1" when any plant is (the game's own status words: one pest, the small black insects, and Unhealthy below health 30). The stages are the game's own: a plant is a seedling before age 21 (its countdown says "Buds in ... Min."), has buds from 21 ("Mature in ... Min.") and is mature from 24. Dead plants are left out of the count and shown after it as "Dead: 1" until you trash them. A "Counts: On" button at the top right hides or shows them (hidden, only the button stays); the game remembers your choice in "Greenhouse Counts.ini" beside the DLL, never in a save. Once you own an extra greenhouse the lines sit under the greenhouse's name and the button moves right of the name. The lines update every frame and are drawn over everything in the greenhouse (tables, pots, plants, bugs, tools), under only what your hand holds, the bottom bar's text and the game's popups. Display only: nothing in the game or your saves changes. Runs as a companion DLL the game loads at start.

files.destination: Plant Tycoon Fix Patcher DLLs/Greenhouse Counts.dll

settings.name: Add unused flowers
settings.summary: Adds the 14 flowers that are in the game's art but never used: 322 new species, reached by Mutation Liquid and breeding.
settings.description: Adds the 14 flower heads that ship in the game's art but no plant uses, as new flowers: Nightingale, Rosetta, Lilac, Veronica, Violetta, Stella, Silvermist, Anagallis, Buttercup, Cerulean, Phalaena, Mirabilis, Indigoberry and Prunus (names by Virtual_Lady and Lorsieab2), 322 new species with the 23 foliages. All are the rarest class. Mutation Liquid can now step a Tilia flower one place further, into the new ones, with the same odds, and breeding with one of them follows the DS fish rule (an odd sum rounds up or down at random). Runs as a companion DLL the game loads at start; each save slot keeps the new species' prices and discoveries in a separate file beside the save. See docs/plant-tycoon-new-flowers-design.md.
settings.warning: Turning this off after new flowers are in a save leaves those plants with flowers the game cannot draw or price. Sell or compost them before switching it off.

settings.name: Add new store upgrades and items
settings.summary: Adds an Upgrades view to the Supplies store with Legendary Seeds (the new flowers), the Radioactive Plant Formula and its Bomb, the Revival Potion, Revita-Seed, Automatic Sprinklers, the Auto-Healer, and the Fourth, Fifth and Sixth Seed Box. Needs Add unused flowers.
settings.description: Adds an Upgrades link on the bricks at the left of the Supplies store. It opens a second view of the store with only the new items, each where it would sit in the store: Legendary Seeds on the seed shelves (three a day, $5000 each, any foliage with one of the unused flowers; the stock seed packets keep their stock flowers), the Radioactive Plant Formula with the chemicals ($10,000, 3 doses, far beyond spamming Fertilizer Bombs and Plant Food: every branch grows, the largest size, full bloom, a flower on every spot of every branch and leaf, no dead or brown leaves, full health, and always 5 seeds: all 5 when it is pollinated later, or, if it is already pollinated, all its seeds ripe at once; and treated plants sell for the highest possible price: when a visitor buys a plant given the formula or its Bomb, in any nursery, you are paid its species' highest selling price, the highest asking price a visitor still buys at with every effect at its best (the Breeding Guide's Highest selling with Max effects), instead of your asking price, while whether and when it sells still follow your asking price; the mark stays with the plant through moves, nurseries and saves, and ends when it is sold, dies or its pot is replanted), the Revival Potion beside it ($10,000, 3 doses: a dead plant it is dropped on comes back to life at full health, and for sale again if it was for sale when it died), Revita-Seed beside that ($2,500, 3 doses: a plant that has given all its seeds can be pollinated again, as a fresh plant can), the Radioactive Plant Formula Bomb under the formula ($30,000, 3 doses: one Radioactive Plant Formula dose for every live plant in the greenhouse on screen, the pots the Fertilizer Bomb reaches, each then treated and selling for the highest price too), Automatic Sprinklers ($10,000) on the tool shelf under the Extra Greenhouse and the Auto-Healer ($10,000) beside the Formula Bomb (each bought once; they work on every live potted plant in every greenhouse, on screen or not, through time away and the Time Warp too: the sprinklers keep the water at 800, never too dry and below the 900 at which pests come three times as often; the Auto-Healer clears pests, each counted under Plants Cured, and keeps health at 100; neither touches a dead plant, and old age still ends a plant's life; unpurchase: click an owned one and answer Yes, it switches off at once with no refund, and buying it again costs the full price; ownership is kept in "Auto Upgrades <slot>.dat"), and the Fourth, Fifth and Sixth Seed Box with the tool upgrades ("Even more space for your seeds!", $1000 each, bought in order like the stock boxes). Each new box opens a 40-seed drawer in a second chest on the Seed Storage screen; the gold arrows on its title bar switch between boxes 1-3 and 4-6, and the greenhouse fills boxes 4-6 once 1-3 are full. Click Supplies in the bottom bar to leave the Upgrades view. Needs Add unused flowers. Each save slot keeps the new data in separate files beside the save. See docs/plant-tycoon-upgrades-design.md.
settings.warning: Turning this off leaves bought Legendary seeds drawn as another seed packet, the formula drawn as an Insta-Grow Vaporbomb that does nothing (the Revival Potion, Revita-Seed and the Formula Bomb as the last stock chemical, doing nothing too), boxes 4-6 hidden with their seeds, and the extra flowers the formula grew drawn away from their plants. Plant or sell the seeds, use up the formula, the Revival Potion, Revita-Seed and the Formula Bomb, sell or compost the plants it was used on, and move seeds out of boxes 4-6 before switching it off.

settings.name: Sort Seeds button
settings.summary: Adds a Sort Seeds button to the Seed Storage screen: sorts every seed by the plant it grows, then its parents, into the unlocked seed boxes in order.
settings.description: Adds a "Sort Seeds" button on the Seed Storage screen's title bar. One click sorts every seed in your unlocked seed box space and packs them from the first slot, left to right and top to bottom: the First Seed Box's drawer fills first, then the Second's and the Third's if you bought them, then the Fourth, Fifth and Sixth with Add new store upgrades and items. Locked drawers stay empty. Order, lowest first: the class of the plant the seed grows (the game's own A, B, C, D rarity), then its foliage, then its flower, then the parents (the seed's own plant, then the pollen donor; unknown "?" parents first). Seeds that tie keep their order. The sort checks that exactly the same seeds come out as went in before it writes anything, never touches the seed tray, and does nothing while you hold a seed. Runs as a companion DLL the game loads at start; saves are unchanged.

settings.name: Optimize Prices button
settings.summary: Adds an Optimize Prices button to the Nursery: it sets every discovered species to its best price per day for your nursery as it is now.
settings.description: Adds an "Optimize Prices" button on the Nursery's bottom bar, at the right. It asks "Set every discovered species to its best price per day?". On Yes, every species you have discovered gets the Breeding Guide's "best per day" asking price, the price that earns the most money over time, worked out in the game with the same maths as the guide for your nursery as it is now: each species' value, the Golden Berries of Wealth, and the visitors your ornaments, magic plants and bug collection bring with all 15 sale spots filled, for a healthy, flowering plant. Then it says how many prices it set. Species you have not discovered keep their prices and nothing else changes; the new prices are the ones you would type yourself, saved with the game as usual. With Unused Flowers on, its new species are included. Runs as a companion DLL the game loads at start; the save layout is unchanged.

settings.name: Time Warp
settings.summary: Adds a Time Warp item to the store's Upgrades screen: $500 to skip 1-72 hours, as if you had been away.
settings.description: Adds a Time Warp item (a clock) to the Supplies store's Upgrades view (Add new store upgrades and items), which this setting turns on. Clicking it asks, in a small Windows popup, how many hours should pass (1 to 72), then asks Yes/No and charges a flat $500. Then every plant ages with every check (water, health, pests, seeds ripening, old age), and the seed shop restocks if it is due, exactly as if you had been away that many real-life hours, with no catch-up cap. Plants or fish can starve, dry out or die along the way, as they would while you were away. Refused while time is stopped. Saves keep their layout.

settings.summary: Every item on the store's Upgrades screen costs $0.
settings.description: Every item on the Supplies store's Upgrades view (Add new store upgrades and items), which this setting turns on, costs $0: Legendary Seeds ($5000), the Radioactive Plant Formula ($10,000), the Revival Potion ($10,000), Revita-Seed ($2,500), the Formula Bomb ($30,000), Automatic Sprinklers ($10,000), the Auto-Healer ($10,000), the Fourth, Fifth and Sixth Seed Box ($1000 each), and the Time Warp clock ($500), Add Money ($950), the Extra Greenhouse ($10,000 each) and the Extra Nursery ($10,000 each) when those settings are on. The price shown says $0 and no money is taken. Everything else stays: Legendary Seeds are still three a day and need room in the seed tray, the formula, the Revival Potion, Revita-Seed and the Formula Bomb need room in the chemical tray, and the seed boxes, extra greenhouses and extra nurseries are still bought in order, once each. settings.name: 5 extra greenhouses
settings.summary: EXPERIMENTAL - USE AT OWN RISK. Five more greenhouses of 15 pots (90 pots in all), bought one by one on the store's Upgrades screen for $10,000 each; gold arrows on the greenhouse screen page through the ones you own, and every pot works exactly like the stock ones. Needs Add new store upgrades and items.
settings.description: EXPERIMENTAL - USE AT OWN RISK. An Extra Greenhouse item on the store's Upgrades screen (tool shelf, beside the Fourth to Sixth Seed Box) sells Greenhouses 2-6 in order, $10,000 each ($0 with Free upgrades), with a tick once all five are yours. Once you own one, gold arrows (the game's own, as on the Seed Storage screen) on both sides of the greenhouse screen page through Greenhouse 1, the stock one, and the ones you own, and the screen says "Greenhouse 2 of 3". Each greenhouse is the stock greenhouse screen, and the game's own code runs on its 15 pots: plants grow, age, need water and care, flower, take pollen, give seeds, get pests and die exactly as in Greenhouse 1, also while you look at another greenhouse or another screen, while you are away (caught up when you come back) and through the Time Warp. Every chemical, tool, upgrade and magic plant works in every greenhouse. Drag a plant onto an arrow to move it to the same pot place in the greenhouse that arrow leads to (or its first empty pot if that place is taken); pollen and seeds you take from a plant are carried along, and tools, chemicals and tray seeds stay in your hand. Plants tagged for sale in any greenhouse go to the nursery; without 5 extra nurseries the game's limit holds: at most 15 plants are for sale at once, counting every greenhouse. Greenhouses 2-6 are kept beside each save in "Plant Tycoon Fix Patcher Data\Extra Greenhouses <slot>.dat"; the save itself keeps the stock layout. Runs as a companion DLL the game loads at start.
settings.warning: Greenhouses 2-6 only exist while this setting is on. Before switching it off, empty them: move every plant to Greenhouse 1, or sell or compost it. Their plants stay in the slot's Extra Greenhouses file and come back if you switch the setting on again.

patches.note: VA 0x42E23B, one byte. The old-age branch rolls Random(1000) and kills the plant when the result is 0-9, a 1 percent chance per eligible update. The comparison operand changes from 9 to 0xFF, which as a signed compare leaves the range empty, so every roll 0-999 skips the health-zero write. The age check at VA 0x42E219 and the RNG call itself are untouched.

The .text section's VirtualSize, 0x6392F -> 0x64000 (its raw size), so the zero tail that holds the new game's flag clear is mapped. R refreshes the seed shop makes the same change, so this copy applies only without it.
VA 0x464950 (the zero tail of .text): clear the seven magic plant flags, state + 0x2180..0x2186 (the bytes 0x41F170 clears later), then jump to the price setup 0x41DBD0.
The new game's price setup call (0x41EFB8) goes through 0x464950, so the prices never read the Flower of Knowledge flag of the save that was open before.

VA 0x464970 (the zero tail of .text): a loaded save that has not found the Flower of Knowledge (state + 0x2181 is 0) but where every species it has not discovered (V >= 4) asks exactly V + 3 x (V/4), the price an earlier save's flag gave its new game, gets those undiscovered species re-priced by the price setup's own rule, V -+ Random(V/2). Discovered species, whose prices the player may have set, and every other field are left alone. Then it jumps to 0x41ED70, where the load was going.
The load's call at 0x41EEF9 (to 0x41ED70, just after the save is copied into the state) goes through 0x464970 first.
The .text section's VirtualSize, 0x6392F -> 0x64000 (its raw size), so the zero tail that holds the R key's code is mapped.
VA 0x464930 (the zero tail of .text): if the typed character is r or R, call the game's own seed-shelf roll 0x41DC60 on the state ([store+0x1BC]); always return 0, as the ignored-key case did.
Case 4 of the store's character switch (jump table 0x4479E0), the ignored keys, now goes through the R key code at 0x464930 instead of straight to 'return 0'.
